name: benchpod
description: Drive a BenchPod hardware-in-the-loop bench: flash, power, UART, I2C sensor emulation, logic and analog capture, CAN.
long_description:
Connects Claude to an [EmbeddedCI BenchPod](https://www.embeddedci.com/docs/benchpod-mcp), a hardware-in-the-loop tester wired to your board. Claude can flash a build over SWD, power-cycle the board and wait for its boot log, type into its UART console, pretend to be the I2C sensor it expects, capture logic and analog signals, drive voltages and talk CAN.

The server runs on your computer and talks to the pod over your network or USB. A cloud pod (`embeddedci:<device>`) needs an embeddedci.com API key.

Tools that switch power, flash firmware or drive voltages are marked destructive, so Claude asks before using them.

Flashing needs OpenOCD with the `cmsis_dap_tcp` backend (newer than 0.12.0, for example `brew install --HEAD open-ocd`) on this computer. Everything else works without it.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Open a BenchPod connection (closing any previous one and its sessions) and report status.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Close UART/CAN sessions and the connection, releasing a cloud lease. Safe when not connected.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Connection, firmware, capabilities, selected LA voltage and open sessions — with warnings for anything that will block the next steps (e.g. no LA voltage). Works when not connected.

tools.name: set_la_voltage
tools.description: Select the LA I/O-bank voltage to match the DUT's I/O (1.8 V needs a rev3 pod).

tools.name: wiring
tools.description: Which DUT signal is on which LA channel — call this first, before any channel argument.

tools.name: set_wiring
tools.description: Replace the wiring profile this connection uses (and optionally store it on embeddedci.com).

tools.name: power_on
tools.description: Switch the target's power rail on. The result says which rail was used.

tools.name: power_off
tools.description: Switch the target's power rail off. The result says which rail was used.

tools.name: measure_power
tools.description: Measure the DUT's supply current and voltage for a window: average, minimum and peak current, voltage, energy and charge (gap-free sampling, so energy is integrated, not estimated).

tools.name: power_profile_start
tools.description: Start sampling the target-power rail in the background, then run the steps you want to profile and call power_profile_stop. Replaces any profile already running.

tools.name: power_profile_stop
tools.description: Stop the running power profile and return its statistics (and, with points, a trace).

tools.name: power_status
tools.description: Both target-power rails: eFuse on/off and tripped state, bus voltage and current draw.

tools.name: reset_target
tools.description: Drive the DUT's reset line from the pod's reset pin (rev3 pods, DUT header J1 pin 22).

tools.name: flash
tools.description: Program the DUT over SWD through the pod's CMSIS-DAP probe (OpenOCD runs on this server's host).

tools.name: capture_uart
tools.description: Record the DUT's UART output for a fixed window (or until until_regex matches).

tools.name: power_cycle_and_capture
tools.description: Power the target off, then capture UART while it powers back on — the boot banner lands in the window.

tools.name: uart_open
tools.description: Start buffering the DUT's UART in the background (replacing any open session).

tools.name: uart_write
tools.description: Send text to the DUT's RX through the open UART session.

tools.name: uart_read
tools.description: Return the UART output received since the previous uart_read, optionally waiting for a match.

tools.name: uart_close
tools.description: Stop the background UART session (safe when none is open).

tools.name: enable_i2c_sensor
tools.description: Make the pod act as a BMP280 on sda/scl for the DUT to read. Engage pull-ups on both lines first (set_pull).

tools.name: set_i2c_sensor
tools.description: Change what the emulated sensor reports (at least one value).

tools.name: disable_i2c_sensor
tools.description: Disarm the emulated sensor (safe when none is active).

tools.name: i2c_sensor_status
tools.description: Emulated sensor state plus bus activity counters — did the DUT talk to it at all?

tools.name: i2c_sensor_regs
tools.description: Read the emulated sensor's register image.

tools.name: i2c_sensor_capture
tools.description: Capture and decode the emulated sensor's I2C bus into a transaction trace (S/Sr/P, addr, data, ACK).

tools.name: set_pull
tools.description: Engage or release the fixed bias resistors: LA1-LA6 pull UP (I2C lines), LA7/LA8 pull DOWN.

tools.name: pull_status
tools.description: State, direction and value of the bias resistor on LA1-LA8.

tools.name: la_pins
tools.description: What owns each of the 14 LA channels — none (free), gpio, uart_rx/uart_tx, swd_clk/swd_dio, i2c_sda/i2c_scl or step — plus each channel's GPIO mode, commanded level and bias resistor.

tools.name: gpio_mode
tools.description: Claim LA channels as GPIO so the pod can drive or read them.

tools.name: gpio_write
tools.description: Set the level of GPIO output / open-drain channels (all of them in one pod command).

tools.name: gpio_read
tools.description: The live level (0/1) of LA channels — omit `la` for all 14.

tools.name: gpio_wait
tools.description: Wait until an LA channel reads `level` (reached=false when the timeout passes first).

tools.name: gpio_pulse
tools.description: Emit FPGA-timed pulses on an LA channel — a trigger for the DUT, or a step/dir motor train.

tools.name: gpio_release
tools.description: Stop using channels as GPIO — they go back to high-Z, watched by captures.

tools.name: analog_path
tools.description: Set every analog mux and relay for a named path in one step.

tools.name: dac_output
tools.description: Route a DAC output (3v3, 5v, 12v = ±12 V, or off) and drive a calibrated DC voltage on it.

tools.name: adc_read
tools.description: One calibrated voltage: ext = front SMA (true volts), cal1/cal2 = DAC loopbacks, amp = current terminal.

tools.name: capture_adc
tools.description: Capture the ADC and summarise it: calibrated stats, dominant frequency and a min/max envelope.

tools.name: capture_la
tools.description: Capture all 14 LA channels and summarise each: levels, edge count, first edge, estimated frequency.

tools.name: capture_correlated
tools.description: ADC and LA captured from one hardware trigger, so their timebases align. Both are kept.

tools.name: decode_la
tools.description: Decode I2C (sda, scl), UART (rx, baud) or SPI (sclk + mosi/miso/cs, mode) from LA data.

tools.name: la_timing
tools.description: Timing of one channel of the last capture_la / capture_correlated: edge timestamps, pulse widths, frequency and duty cycle; with to_la, the delay from its first edge to the next edge on to_la (e.g. a trigger pin to a "result ready" pin). Resolution is one sample; no new capture is taken.

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Drive a sine, square or sawtooth on a DAC output (built from 8-bit levels).

tools.name: dac_stop
tools.description: Stop any DAC output: generator, replay or control loop.

tools.name: replay
tools.description: Loop a waveform out of the DAC until dac_stop — agent-provided volts or the last ADC capture.

tools.name: list_waveforms
tools.description: The organisation's cloud waveform library (needs a cloud connection or BENCHPOD_API_KEY).

tools.name: replay_waveform
tools.description: Loop a cloud-library waveform out of the DAC until dac_stop (needs server access).

tools.name: save_capture_as_recording
tools.description: Save the last capture_adc to the cloud waveform library as a replayable recording.

tools.name: control_loop
tools.description: Run a tabulated transfer function in the FPGA: each tick out = curve[input], damped and clamped.

tools.name: loop_input
tools.description: Re-target the running loop's input without re-arming (hold a point, meter, move on).

tools.name: loop_probe
tools.description: The running loop's live operating point; assert against loop_input, not i, in open-loop runs.

tools.name: fpga_image
tools.description: Reprogram the pod's FPGA with another stored gateware image (~2-3 s).

tools.name: can_open
tools.description: Bring up the pod's CAN interface (replacing any open CAN session).

tools.name: can_write
tools.description: Queue one classic CAN frame.

tools.name: can_read
tools.description: Read received CAN frames (id, data, timestamps in pod milliseconds).

tools.name: can_respond
tools.description: Make the pod firmware answer a CAN id instantly (ECU simulation), or clear all rules.

tools.name: can_status
tools.description: CAN link state: mode, bitrate, error counters, bus-off.

tools.name: can_close
tools.description: Clear responder rules and stop CAN (safe when not open).

tools.name: la_step
tools.description: Emit step pulses on an LA channel (step/dir motor drivers); with dir_la, set direction first.

tools.name: command
tools.description: Escape hatch for firmware commands no tool covers. Prefer the dedicated tools.

connection.title: BenchPod connection
connection.description: The pod's IP address or host[:port] on your network, or embeddedci:<device-name> for a cloud pod. Leave empty to give it to Claude in chat.

la_voltage.title: Board I/O voltage
la_voltage.description: The board's I/O voltage: 3.3 or 1.8. Leave empty and Claude sets it before using the pins.

api_key.title: embeddedci.com API key
api_key.description: Needed only for cloud pods and the waveform library. Create one at https://www.embeddedci.com/api-keys.
